clue.text: Answer objection about

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Answer objection about (8)': A + BUT accounts for four letters, nothing gives ILON; the clue is cut short in the OCR.

clue.text: Hill, very big, to climb — work not finished

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters are read upwards, so this piece runs backwards

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A climber sets out to scale a huge hill but abandons the effort halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' turns OS into SO in this down clue. A torso is a sculpture of a body without head or limbs, so it is work left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted trunk lacking head and limbs is the classic example of an unfinished artwork.

clue.text: Problem with damage of for magistrates' court

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Problem with damage of for magistrates' court (7,7)' is garbled: no anagram or charade of these words gives the answer, and words are plainly missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Problem with damage of for magistrates' court

clue.text: A label on vehicle is to show it's from here?

definitions.text: A label on vehicle is to show it's from here?

parts.words: A label on vehicle is to show it's from here?
parts.note: the letter A on an international vehicle plate marks a car registered in a particular alpine country

explanation.surface: A sticker on a car is there to tell everyone where it comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: International oval plates carry country codes; a car showing the single letter A comes from Vienna's country.
explanation.definitionFit: The international vehicle registration code A belongs to the alpine republic, so the label points to that nation.

clue.text: Fellow in happy mood brought about by loud commendation

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the word for the happy mood runs backwards

parts.note: to be up is to be cheerful
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A man cheered by hearty praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' turns UP into PU, followed by the two F's.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is a piece of extravagant praise, the kind a publicist writes for a book's cover.

clue.text: Speechless, upset about part after start of play being crude?

indicators.note: after says this group of letters follows the opening one
the start of a word is its first letter, here taken from play
about means the upset word goes around the part
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for speechless is read backwards

parts.note: mute means unable to speak
an actor's role is the part played

explanation.surface: An actor struck dumb and rattled by their role at the start of the play seems unpolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the word for speechless in this down clue, 'about' wraps it round the part, and 'after start of play' puts P first. 'crude' is the noun, unrefined oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil is the unrefined mineral oil drawn from wells, before refining into fuels.

clue.text: Hunt's opponent ringing newspaper

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the opponent encircles the newspaper

parts.note: a foe is an enemy or opponent
rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to fox hunting telephones the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt's' reads as the hunt's opponent, a saboteur; in fact it is 'Hunt is', with the verb as definition. 'ringing' puts the newspaper inside the opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search about for food or supplies, a kind of hunting.

clue.text: Accommodation achieved by modernist and bigot after a struggle

indicators.note: a struggle throws things about, so these two words are jumbled together into new order

explanation.surface: Someone finds lodging only after a fight between a modernist and a bigot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a struggle' rearranges all fourteen fodder letters. A bedsit is a single rented room for living and sleeping, common in British cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room rented flat combining bedroom and living space is a basic form of lodging.

clue.text: See meeting, lacking force, given up without it at the outset?

definitions.text: See meeting, lacking force, given up without it at the outset?

parts.words: See meeting, lacking force, given up without it at the outset?
parts.note: a gathering cannot make binding decisions and is abandoned when the minimum number of members is not present when it begins

explanation.surface: A church assembly lacks authority and is called off before it starts.
explanation.walkthrough: A meeting without enough members present at the start has no power to decide anything and must be abandoned. 'See' points to a diocesan gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum attendance needed for a body's decisions to be valid is checked at the start of proceedings.

clue.text: Officer protected by nothing other than screen

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed inside it

parts.note: sheer means utter or mere, as in sheer luck
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An officer is kept safe by nothing more than a curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts the officer inside the word for nothing other than; 'screen' is the verb, to shield.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen something is to protect or hide it, which is what giving cover does.

clue.text: Miserable and sour, I may be seen as unadaptable type

indicators.note: miserable suggests something in a wretched state, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A grumpy, sour man says people will think him stuck in his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miserable' rearranges AND, SOUR and I. Calling a person a fossil of this kind means they refuse to move with the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a person who will not change with the times is likened to an extinct prehistoric reptile.

clue.text: Cast of in marshy area

definitions.meaning: a snake sheds or casts off its skin

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to shed dead skin, and the noun names a boggy hollow of wet ground.

clue.text: Structure used in play truncated certain series of events involving a saint

indicators.note: a truncated word has lost its end, here the final letter of the word for certain

parts.note: bound means certain, as in bound to happen

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the series of events encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a cycle is a recurring series of events

explanation.surface: A theatrical set gets cut, a series of events involving a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'truncated' drops the last letter of the word for certain; 'involving' puts A and the saint inside the series. 'play' means children's play, not drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable castle is a children's plaything for jumping on at fairs and parties.

clue.text: Pieces of meat I prepared in minutes

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the record of a meeting

parts.note: the minutes of a meeting are notes of it
set means prepared, as in all set

explanation.surface: A cook prepares meat cuts in a matter of minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and the word for prepared inside the minutes. 'minutes' are a meeting's record, not units of time.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small round boneless cuts of lamb or similar, served as individual portions.

clue.text: One who makes records shrink for the auditor?

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as heard

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist or psychoanalyst

explanation.surface: A record-keeper tells an accountant about a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but means a listener. Said aloud, the word for a psychoanalyst matches a chronicler who keeps yearly records.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler who writes yearly historical accounts keeps records of events year by year.

clue.text: It incorporates news in which aim often is to be funny

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'It incorporates news in which aim often is to be funny (12)': IT around an anagram of IN AIM OFTEN gives an I where the answer needs a third N, and adding N for 'news' gives one letter too many; no reading accounts for every letter.
annotationWithheld.clue: It incorporates news in which aim often is to be funny

clue.text: Right away, name troublesome person, creating storm

indicators.note: away means sent off, so the letter for right is dropped from the word for name

parts.note: a term is a name for something
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone at once names a nuisance who stirs things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' removes R from TERM to leave TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent storm with high winds is a gale, as in Shakespeare's play title.

clue.text: In store, look for a hat

indicators.note: in places the word for look inside the store

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A shopper goes into a shop to look for a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts LO inside CACHE (C-LO-CHE). 'store' is a hoard, not a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a close-fitting bell-shaped women's hat popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: Rook left in charge around end of game

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the word for charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
c, for circa, means around when giving dates

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here from game

explanation.surface: A chess rook stays in charge until the end of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the chess piece but is the verb meaning to cheat. 'in' puts L inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle them, charging far too much.

clue.text: Satisfied about talk with artist recalled as very famous person

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for satisfied encloses the talk

parts.note: met means satisfied, as in met the demand
gas is idle talk or chatter

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the abbreviation for artist runs backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone pleased to chat with a painter remembers them as a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the satisfied word round the talk; 'recalled' turns the artist backwards. RA is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity of the highest order is a huge star of stage or screen.

clue.text: Peaceful negotiations ultimately work

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, pointing to the last letter of negotiations

parts.note: to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: Calm talks finally do their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the S that ends 'negotiations'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and motionless, without disturbance, is a quiet, tranquil state.

clue.text: Saw water in frozen state, covering lake, forming layer

parts.note: to saw is to cut

indicators.note: covering means going over and around, so the frozen water wraps the lake

parts.note: frozen water is ice

explanation.surface: Someone sees a frozen lake covered with a layer of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of 'see' but is the verb to cut. 'covering' puts L inside ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin outer skin at the base of a fingernail, or any protective outer coating, is a covering layer.

clue.text: Love outfit with modish provenance

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
a rig is an outfit of clothes
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A lover of fashionable clothes asks where they came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Where something comes from is its source or starting point.

clue.text: Part of optical instrument used by naval ensign

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A junior naval officer uses a telescope at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'navaL ENSign'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaped piece of glass that focuses light is the key component of a telescope or microscope.

clue.text: Office worker supplied by agency? Former model

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker placed by an employment agency
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: An agency temp used to be a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' sounds like the temp's old job, but it is a pattern to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern used as a guide for making copies serves as a model.
